title: Aaron Journeys Toward Jerusalem
summary: Ammon and his brethren separate in the borders of the land of the Lamanites. Aaron then journeys toward the land called Jerusalem by the Lamanites.
locations: Borders of the land of the Lamanites

explicit_facts.text: Ammon and his brethren separated themselves in the borders of the land of the Lamanites.
Aaron took his journey toward the land called Jerusalem by the Lamanites.
Jerusalem was away joining the borders of Mormon.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Aaron traveling separately after the group parts.
unspecified_visual_details: The travelers' appearances and clothing.
The landscape, route, and distance.

narration.text: Aaron took his journey towards the land which was called by the Lamanites, Jerusalem

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lamanites called the land Jerusalem after the land of their fathers’ nativity.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Ammon or the other brethren accompanying Aaron on his journey.
Do not invent a visible city, conversation, or additional events.

title: Jerusalem and Its People
summary: The Lamanites, Amalekites, and people of Amulon had built the great city called Jerusalem. The Amalekites and Amulonites caused the Lamanites to harden their hearts and grow strong in wickedness and abominations.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites, Amalekites, and people of Amulon had built a great city called Jerusalem.
The Amalekites and Amulonites were harder than the Lamanites and caused them to harden their hearts and wax strong in wickedness and abominations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jerusalem can be shown as an established city.
unspecified_visual_details: The city's architecture, layout, and appearance.
The people's clothing and physical appearance.

narration.text: Now the Lamanites and the Amalekites and the people of Amulon had built a great city, which was called Jerusalem.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The building is reported as already completed; do not depict it as a new construction event.
Hardened hearts and wickedness are described, not narrated as a visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific act of wickedness not stated in the verses.
Do not invent speech or a visible event to represent the hardening of hearts.

title: Aaron Preaches in a Synagogue
summary: Aaron comes to Jerusalem and begins preaching to the Amalekites in their synagogues.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron came to the city of Jerusalem and first began to preach to the Amalekites.
Aaron began to preach to them in their synagogues.
The Amalekites had built synagogues after the order of the Nehors; many Amalekites and Amulonites were after that order.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Aaron preaching to Amalekites inside a synagogue.
unspecified_visual_details: The synagogue’s appearance and furnishings.
The people’s clothing and arrangement.

narration.text: And he began to preach to them in their synagogues,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not describe visual features of the order of the Nehors.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Nehor as physically present or invent Aaron’s sermon.

title: An Amalekite Challenges Aaron
summary: Aaron enters a synagogue and speaks to the people. An Amalekite arises and contends with him, questioning his testimony, repentance, and the people's righteousness, worship, and belief that God will save all men.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron entered one of their synagogues to preach to the people and was speaking to them.
An Amalekite arose and began to contend with Aaron.
The Amalekite asked about Aaron's testimony, angels, and whether the people were as good as Aaron's people.
The Amalekite questioned the need for repentance and the judgment of the people's righteousness; he said they had built sanctuaries, assembled to worship God, and believed God would save all men.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Amalekite stands while addressing Aaron.
unspecified_visual_details: The synagogue's architecture, clothing, expressions, and gestures.

spoken_dialogue.text: How knowest thou that we have cause to repent?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, we have built sanctuaries, and we do assemble ourselves together to worship God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

spoken_dialogue.text: We do believe that God will save all men.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

narration.text: as Aaron entered into one of their synagogues to preach unto the people
there arose an Amalekite and began to contend with him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statements about sanctuaries, worship, and salvation are the Amalekite's claims, not independently narrated facts.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an angel; the Amalekite only asks about one.
Do not depict the sanctuaries being built or a separate worship gathering.
Do not give Aaron unquoted dialogue.

title: Aaron Questions the Amalekite
summary: Aaron asks whether the man believes the Son of God will come to redeem mankind from their sins. The man rejects Aaron’s knowledge and what he calls foolish traditions.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron asked the man whether he believed the Son of God would come to redeem mankind from their sins.
The man said they did not believe Aaron knew such things, rejected the traditions, and denied knowledge of things to come by Aaron’s fathers or their own.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Aaron and the Amalekite continue their exchange in the synagogue.
unspecified_visual_details: The speakers’ expressions and gestures.

spoken_dialogue.text: Believest thou that the Son of God shall come to redeem mankind from their sins?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Aaron

spoken_dialogue.text: We do not believe that thou knowest any such thing.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

spoken_dialogue.text: We do not believe in these foolish traditions.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

spoken_dialogue.text: We do not believe that thou knowest of things to come,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The man’s words continue through the rest of Alma 21:8; the scene’s spoken text uses only short exact excerpts.

title: Aaron Opens the Scriptures
summary: Aaron opens the scriptures and expounds teachings about Christ, resurrection, and redemption. His listeners become angry, mock him, and refuse to hear him.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron began to open the scriptures concerning the coming of Christ, the resurrection of the dead, and redemption through Christ’s death, sufferings, and atonement.
As Aaron began to expound these things, his listeners became angry, mocked him, and would not hear him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Aaron consulting scriptures while teaching.
Listeners visibly reacting as they mock Aaron.
unspecified_visual_details: The scriptures’ physical form.
The listeners’ appearance and specific gestures.
The setting’s appearance.

narration.text: Now Aaron began to open the scriptures unto them concerning the coming of Christ,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize Aaron’s teaching but provide no direct quotation of his speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ’s coming, resurrection, or atonement as events occurring in this scene.
Do not invent Aaron’s words, the listeners’ words, or a specific location.

title: Arrival at Ani-Anti
summary: After seeing that his listeners would not hear his words, Aaron departed from their synagogue and came to Ani-Anti. He found Muloki preaching the word, and also Ammah and his brethren. The verse reports contention with many about the word without specifying everyone included in “they.”

explicit_facts.text: The arriving man had departed from their synagogue after seeing that they would not hear his words.
He came to a village called Ani-Anti, where he found Muloki preaching the word, and also Ammah and his brethren.
The verse states that “they” contended with many about the word, without explicitly enumerating that group's members.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Stage the arrival at Ani-Anti with Aaron encountering Muloki preaching and Ammah and his brethren present.
Listeners may be positioned near Muloki without assigning individual reactions.
unspecified_visual_details: Village layout and architecture.
Clothing, ages, and physical appearances.
The number of listeners and brethren.

narration.text: And they contended with many about the word.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Aaron is the continuity label established by the preceding scene as identified in the correction; this verse itself uses “he.”
Keep the earlier synagogue departure distinct from the arrival at Ani-Anti.
Retain the contention as a reported event rather than staging a newly invented exchange.
No words from the preaching or contention are supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent preaching or contention dialogue.
Do not identify every participant meant by “they.”
Do not depict physical fighting based on contention about the word.
Do not place the earlier synagogue departure and the village encounter in one simultaneous setting.
Do not give unnamed listeners or brethren names, biographies, or motives.

title: To the Land of Middoni
summary: They see that the people would harden their hearts, depart for the land of Middoni, and preach the word to many. Few believe what they teach.

explicit_facts.text: They saw that the people would harden their hearts.
They departed and came to the land of Middoni.
They preached the word to many, and few believed what they taught.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The departure and the preaching can be shown as successive moments.
The preaching may be shown before a group of listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The place they departed from and their route to Middoni.
The identities and appearances of the preachers, listeners, and few believers.

narration.text: And they did preach the word unto many, and few believed on the words which they taught.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports preaching but gives no words spoken by the preachers.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the preachers or their place of departure.
Do not invent a sermon or identify which listeners believed.
Do not depict hardened hearts as a literal visible event.

title: Aaron and Others Imisoned
summary: Aaron and some of his brethren are taken and cast into prison. The remainder flee from the land of Middoni to the surrounding regions.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron and a certain number of his brethren were taken and cast into prison.
The remainder fled out of the land of Middoni unto the regions round about.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Some of the brethren could be shown entering confinement; others could be shown departing the land of Middoni.
unspecified_visual_details: The captors' identities and appearances.
The prison's appearance and the exact number of brethren.

narration.text: Nevertheless, Aaron and a certain number of his brethren were taken and cast into prison, and the remainder of them fled out of the land of Middoni unto the regions round about.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the captors or add dialogue.
Do not depict the imprisonment and flight as necessarily simultaneous.

title: The Prisoners Are Delivered
summary: Those cast into prison suffer many things. Lamoni and Ammon deliver them, and they are fed and clothed. Afterward, they go forth again to declare the word.

explicit_facts.text: Those cast into prison suffered many things.
Lamoni and Ammon delivered them.
They were fed and clothed.
They went forth again to declare the word after their first deliverance from prison.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The released people may be shown receiving food and clothing.
Their departure to declare the word follows their deliverance rather than occurring at the same moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The nature of their suffering.
The method of their release.
The prison’s appearance and location.
The appearance of the food and clothing.

narration.text: And those who were cast into prison suffered many things
And they went forth again to declare the word

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses do not name the imprisoned people or describe how Lamoni and Ammon delivered them.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give the prisoners invented names or assign the prison a location.
Do not depict specific mistreatment, injuries, or a method of release.
Do not invent spoken words for their declaration.

title: Preaching in Synagogues and Assemblies
summary: They go forth where led by the Spirit of the Lord and preach in Amalekite synagogues and Lamanite assemblies where admitted. The Lord begins to bless them; they bring many to knowledge of the truth and convince many of their sins and incorrect traditions.

explicit_facts.text: They went where they were led by the Spirit of the Lord and preached where they could be admitted.
The Lord began to bless them, and they brought many to knowledge of the truth and convinced many of their sins and incorrect traditions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A preacher addressing gathered listeners in an assembly where admitted.
unspecified_visual_details: Which particular synagogue or assembly is shown.
The appearance of the preachers and listeners.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's blessing is reported; no visible appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the preachers or invent their words.
Do not depict the Lord or the Spirit appearing.
Do not stage distinct gatherings or later outcomes as one simultaneous event.

title: Ammon and Lamoni Return to Ishmael
summary: Ammon and Lamoni return from the land of Middoni to the land of Ishmael. King Lamoni does not allow Ammon to serve him or be his servant.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon and Lamoni returned from the land of Middoni to the land of Ishmael, the land of their inheritance.
King Lamoni would not allow Ammon to serve him or be his servant.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon and Lamoni traveling toward the land of Ishmael.
unspecified_visual_details: Their route and means of travel.
How Lamoni expresses his refusal.

narration.text: And it came to pass that Ammon and Lamoni returned from the land of Middoni to the land of Ishmael, which was the land of their inheritance.
And king Lamoni would not suffer that Ammon should serve him, or be his servant.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: No direct dialogue is supplied for Lamoni’s refusal.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent words spoken by Lamoni or Ammon.

title: Synagogues and Assembly
summary: A ruler causes synagogues to be built in the land of Ishmael and causes the people under his reign to assemble.

explicit_facts.text: He caused synagogues to be built in the land of Ishmael.
He caused the people under his reign to assemble together.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Synagogue buildings in the land of Ishmael.
People gathering together.
unspecified_visual_details: The synagogues’ appearance and construction materials.
The size and appearance of the assembly.

narration.text: But he caused that there should be synagogues built in the land of Ishmael;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The ruler is not named in the supplied verse.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the ruler or invent a speech or ceremony.
Do not assume the assembly takes place inside a synagogue.

title: Lamoni Teaches His People
summary: Lamoni rejoices over the people and teaches them. He declares that they are free from his father’s oppression and may worship the Lord according to their desires in the land under his reign.

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni rejoiced over the people and taught them many things.
He declared that the people were free from the oppression of his father, who had granted him rule over the land of Ishmael and the surrounding land.
He declared that they could worship the Lord according to their desires in any place within the land under his reign.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamoni addressing the people he teaches.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact place where Lamoni teaches the people.
His gestures and the people's appearance.

narration.text: And he did rejoice over them, and he did teach them many things.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report Lamoni’s declarations rather than quote his speech directly.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Lamoni’s father as present.
Do not invent dialogue for Lamoni or details of the teachings summarized in the verses.

title: Ammon Teaches Lamoni’s People
summary: Ammon preaches to the people of king Lamoni, teaches them about righteousness, and exhorts them daily. They heed his word and are zealous to keep God’s commandments.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon preached to the people of king Lamoni and taught them concerning righteousness.
Ammon exhorted them daily with diligence.
The people heeded his word and were zealous for keeping God’s commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon addressing a group of listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and listeners’ appearances.

narration.text: And Ammon did preach unto the people of king Lamoni;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse summarizes repeated teaching and the people’s response; it supplies no sermon wording.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent Ammon’s sermon or depict the daily exhortations as a single continuous event.
